newsitem.title: USA: Clinton speaks to Netanyahu on Mideast peace moves. [CORRECTED 21:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Clinton speaks to Netanyahu on Mideast peace moves. [CORRECTED 21:30 GMT]

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton conferred by telephone with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Tuesday (corrects from Thursday) on ways to push forward the Middle East peace process, the White House said.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry said the call, initiated by Netanyahu, "obviously was aimed at encouraging progress in the discussions about implementation of the Oslo accords (on Middle East peace)." He declined to discuss specifics.

Netanyahu made the call after a visit to Israel by French President Jacques Chirac, who has strongly criticised the Israeli leader's commitment to expanding Jewish settlement in the West Bank and his refusal to relinquish Israel's hold over Arab East Jerusalem.

Chirac has been touring the region in a drive to increase French and European political influence on Arab-Israeli peace negotiations, calling for the European Union to co-sponsor the peace process with the United States.

Netanyahu visited Washington earlier this month for an emergency summit with Clinton, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Jordan's King Hussein that effectively halted an upsurge of Israeli-Palestinian violence that killed 60 Arabs and 15 Israelis last month.

That summit led to a fresh direct Israeli-Palestinian talks, mediated by the United States, on implementing outstanding Palestinian self-rule agreements, including the redeployment of Israeli troops around Hebron in the West Bank.
